subtopics.title: The Adjustments That Make the Year True

questions.question: Total depreciation for the year is:
options: R8 900 — vehicle R8 000 (20% straight-line on R40 000) plus equipment R900 (10% of carrying value R9 000)
R9 000 — taking 10% of the equipment's cost instead of its carrying value

questions.question: Water and electricity paid R2 400 with February's R400 unpaid means:
options: Expense R2 800, and R400 stands as a current liability — accrued expense
Expense R2 000, and R400 as income

questions.question: Insurance paid R1 800 including R300 for next year gives:
options: Expense R1 800 and a liability of R300
Expense R1 500, with prepaid insurance R300 as a current asset

questions.question: Every adjustment performs the same two-sided move:
options: Correct the income/expense to the TRUE year figure and park the difference on the statement of financial position

subtopics.title: From Final Accounts to the Two Statements

questions.question: The trading account shows:
options: Sales R120 000 against cost of sales R80 000 — gross profit R40 000, matching the 50% mark-up on cost

questions.question: Net profit for the year is:
options: R14 800 — gross profit 40 000 plus rent income 6 000 less operating expenses 31 200

questions.question: Owner's equity at year-end is:
options: R78 000 — opening 70 000 plus profit 14 800 less drawings 6 800

questions.question: The statement of financial position balances at:
options: R85 700 — non-current assets 70 300 plus current assets 15 400, equal to equity 78 000 plus current liabilities 7 700

questions.question: Gross profit on cost of 50% exactly matching the mark-up policy suggests:
options: No stock leaked unrecorded — the policy held all year

questions.question: The current ratio and acid test are:
Return on equity of 20% is judged by:
options: Whether it is a round number
Comparison — several times what a bank pays on savings, rewarding effort and risk

questions.question: The technique for every interpretation comment is:
options: Quote as many ratios as possible
Figure, comparison, judgement — never a number left naked

subtopics.title: Guards, Rules and the Cost of One Unit

questions.question: Division of duties means:
options: The one who records is not the one who banks — no hand touches money end to end

questions.question: Prudence, as a GAAP principle, requires:
options: Combining the owner's and the business's affairs

questions.question: The unit cost of a shirt is:
options: R12 — materials 6 000 plus labour 4 000 plus overheads 2 000, over 1 000 shirts

questions.question: The mini cash budget closes at:
options: R2 500 — receipts 9 000 less payments 7 500 is surplus 1 500, plus opening 1 000

subtopics.title: Tidying the Room Before the Photo

questions.question: Depreciation is "R8 900 of honesty" because:
options: The books admit the wearing of assets — truth arrives though no cash moves
It is paid to the bank yearly
It is optional for small shops

questions.question: The insurance paid ahead is pushed OUT of the photo because:
options: It belongs to next year — the shop still OWNS that cover, a current asset of R300

questions.question: An untidied photo matters because:
options: It flatters or slanders — skipping depreciation makes the shop look richer than it is, and readers must trust the picture

subtopics.title: The Report Card and the Health Check

questions.question: The report card's three floors are:
options: The buying-and-selling game (R40 000), other income joining (R6 000), and running costs subtracted to the true mark (R14 800)

questions.question: "Ninety-six cents for every rand — just short" describes:
options: The acid test — near money without selling stock against near debts, worth watching

questions.question: "Numbers alone say nothing; numbers COMPARED say everything" means:
options: Every comment needs a comparison — last year, the policy, the bank, the danger line — before a judgement

subtopics.title: Locks on the Doors, and What One Vetkoek Costs

questions.question: The tuck shop where one person takes, counts, records and banks the money is:
options: An invitation — no independent check exists; split the jobs and number the slips
Fine if the person is family

questions.question: Ethics matters beneath the locks because:
options: Rules cannot save books kept by a dishonest hand — the ethics list is the foundation the locks stand on

questions.question: One vetkoek costs:
options: R12 — ingredients 6 000, hands 4 000, stall and gas 2 000, over a thousand vetkoek — leaving R3 each at a R15 price

questions.question: The three street laws under the year's formats are:
options: Sell cheap, buy dear, borrow often
Record only cash, skip the counting, trust memory
Guard the money with split hands and slips; know what one unit truly costs; write the month before living it
